successCriteria.description: The LeaveBalance entity interface extends BaseEntity and exposes the balance domain attributes (employeeId, leavePolicyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, fiscalYear, status as a string-literal union of ACTIVE/EXHAUSTED/CLOSED) plus a read-only derived remainingDays field — all importable from the balance module's barrel.

The repository create call persists a new leave_balances row (generating id/createdAt/updatedAt server-side) and returns a fully-hydrated LeaveBalance whose remainingDays equals totalEntitlement - usedDays.

findByEmployeeAndPolicy returns the single LeaveBalance matching the employee+policy+fiscalYear triple, or null when no row matches; findByEmployeeId returns all balances for an employee in a given fiscalYear (empty array when none).

updateUsedDays performs a single atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING * that sets used_days and updated_at for the given id, returning the updated LeaveBalance with remainingDays recomputed, or null when no row matches the id.

Every read path (findByEmployeeAndPolicy, findByEmployeeId, create, updateUsedDays) hydrates remainingDays as totalEntitlement - usedDays at query time; no INSERT or UPDATE statement references a remaining_days column.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/balance/balance.repository.test.ts mock the shared pg pool and cover success, null/empty, and error paths for every repository method, following the established test pattern from the policy/employee repository tests.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository); the balance repository is the only component that touches the leave_balances table.
Strict TypeScript with no implicit any and strict null checks; use unknown with type guards instead of any (HARNESS no-any rule).

remainingDays is a derived field computed as totalEntitlement - usedDays at query time and must never be written to the database; binding rule #5 takes precedence over the sql_schemas listing of a remaining_days column.
BaseEntity must be imported from the deep path ../../shared/types/base-entity.interface (not the shared barrel), matching the established employee and policy module pattern.
The status field must use a string-literal union ('ACTIVE' | 'EXHAUSTED' | 'CLOSED') without importing an enum, since no existing enum covers these statuses.

updateUsedDays must use a single atomic UPDATE ... SET used_days = $1, updated_at = $2 WHERE id = $3 RETURNING * statement rather than a read-then-write pattern, to prevent race conditions during concurrent deduction/restoration.
Test files must use the project's Jest convention (*.test.ts under tests/), not .spec.ts, and must not change the Jest config.
No unhandled promise rejections (GP-006); all async repository errors must propagate as rejected promises that callers can catch.
outOfScope: Balance service, controller, and routes — deferred to a later phase, matching the employee/policy module phase pattern.
Database migrations for the leave_balances table — not created in this phase.
Audit record writing for balance mutations (GP-002) — deferred; the repository layer does not write audit records in this phase.
RBAC enforcement on balance operations (GP-005) — deferred to the controller/service phase; the repository has no auth context.
Balance accrual logic, carry-over rules, and cross-fiscal-year allocation — open questions deferred per the reconciled architecture.

entityInvariants.invariant: usedDays is the denormalized source-of-truth counter; it is the only persisted consumption value. remainingDays is never persisted and is always derived as totalEntitlement - usedDays on every read.
A LeaveBalance is uniquely identified by the composite key (employeeId, leavePolicyId, fiscalYear); findByEmployeeAndPolicy resolves at most one balance for that triple.

status is constrained to the lifecycle values ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, or CLOSED; the repository does not mutate status in this phase (status transitions are a service-layer concern deferred to a later phase).

LeaveBalance extends BaseEntity, inheriting id (string), createdAt (Date), and updatedAt (Date); create generates id via randomUUID and sets createdAt/updatedAt server-side, matching the employee/policy pattern.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when no matching row exists; rejects the promise on a pool/connection error (propagates, no swallow).
Returns an empty array when no rows match (never null); rejects the promise on a pool/connection error.
Generates id/createdAt/updatedAt server-side and returns the persisted entity with remainingDays hydrated; rejects on a unique-constraint violation or pool error.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth context at the repository layer; RBAC is enforced upstream (deferred to controller/service phase).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Single atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING *; returns null when no row matches the id; rejects on a pool error. Must not perform a read-then-write.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: LeaveBalance must extend the BaseEntity interface exactly as defined (id: string, createdAt: Date, updatedAt: Date) — import from the deep path, not the shared barrel.

The balance repository must follow the established repository pattern: a private *Row interface for snake_case DB columns, a rowTo* mapper converting to the camelCase entity, a Pg*Repository class implementing the I*Repository interface, and use of the shared pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts.
The balance barrel (index.ts) must export the model type, the repository interface type, and the concrete repository class, matching the export shape used by the policy and employee barrels.

The balance repository test must follow the established test pattern: jest.mock the shared db/connection module, mock pool.query, provide makeRow/makeEntity helpers, and cover success, null/empty, and error (pool rejection) paths for each method.

The LeaveBalance entity shape must match the reconciled architecture's domain entity definition (employeeId, leavePolicyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status union, plus BaseEntity fields); remainingDays is listed as an attribute but binding rule #5 mandates it be computed, not stored.

integrationPoints.why: The PgLeaveBalanceRepository executes all SQL through the shared pool, matching the employee and policy repositories.
LeaveBalance extends BaseEntity; the deep-path import establishes the shared-types ← balance dependency declared in the reconciled dependency map.

The leave service will consume ILeaveBalanceRepository for sufficiency checks (remainingDays >= days), atomic deduction on submit (updateUsedDays), and restoration on reject/cancel — this phase delivers the contract that integration depends on.
